method: LLM-assisted read-only triage of current production output against original forecast/criteria; parent spot-checked; NOT criterion qualification

cases.title: Sweeping ammonia changes the composition of a basic buffer
cases.evidence: Step 11 sweep exports only 6.92e-7 mol NH3 (plus N2/O2/CO2 headspace) and the 120 s wait adds no further transfer; swept pH 9.287908 vs sealed control 9.286276, i.e. slightly higher, not lower.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; still one-shot headspace export with competing CO2 removal
cases.next_step: Implement continuous dissolved-to-sweep NH3/CO2 transfer during wait (lane 2 of post-hydrolysis-gap-lanes) and rerun the unchanged original once.

cases.title: Amphiprotic bicarbonate in acid and base arms
cases.evidence: Steps 1/5 NaHCO3 dissolution in the open vessel evolves 7.73e-5 mol CO2 before sealing, so closed carbon is ~0.923 mmol not 1 mmol; acid arm pH 6.72 with CO2(g) 2.32e-4, base arm pH 10.27 with CO3-2 5.23e-4 (C1 directionally met, C2 fails).
cases.next_step: Keep held; record that the C1 speciation contrast holds but the original 1 mmol closed-carbon criterion is contradicted by the open-before-seal protocol.

cases.title: Chemical removal of Ag+ alters electrode potential
cases.evidence: Step 8 precipitates 9.994e-5 mol AgCl leaving Ag+ 5.588e-8 mol, but step 9 cell returns no_cell 'v2 has Ag but none of its ion in solution'.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; same low-activity cell admission gap
cases.next_step: Fix the cell instrument to admit a solved nonzero low Ag+ activity (no global threshold lowering) and report the Nernst EMF.

cases.title: Equal iron totals, unequal oxidising power
cases.evidence: KI is 'not-speciated' in both arms (steps 3/8); final v0 keeps Fe+3 4e-4 and KI(aqueous) 1e-3 with no I2 and charge -0.002.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; iodide/iodine family ownership still missing
cases.next_step: Add an atom/charge-owned KI -> K+ + I- mapping and Fe(III)/I- redox authority, then rerun original.

cases.title: Fe(II)/permanganate 5:1 titration
cases.evidence: Titration ends with Fe+3 9.989e-4, Fe+2 1.109e-6, Mn+2 2e-4, MnO4- 2e-6 persisting, but redox solver reports 'no electron activity ... balances this beaker' and final charge -0.0084.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; same ~1.1 umol Fe(II) / charge mismatch
cases.next_step: Give one authority for Mn/Fe electron transfer with owned charge refresh, then recheck endpoint and charge closure.

cases.title: Carbonate vs bicarbonate acid dose before fizzing
cases.evidence: First 0.5 mmol HCl (steps 7/8): carbonate arm CO2 1.07e-7 mol vs bicarbonate arm 2.30e-4 (C1 met); but bicarbonate arm lost 7.73e-5 mol CO2 before sealing, final C 0.924 vs ~1.00 mmol (C2 fails).
cases.next_step: Keep held as original setup contradiction; do not substitute a post-loss carbon budget.

cases.title: Different catalyst masses, same nominal surface area
cases.evidence: Both grinds give 1.1928e-4 m2, but 100 um particles settle fully (separated_fraction 1.0) in 10 s vs 0.062 for 10 um; O2 after 30 s is 1.177e-5 vs 4.816e-6.
cases.next_step: Keep held; the settling/available-area confound is legitimate physics, not a defect.

cases.title: Splitting a reacting solution preserves fractional kinetics
cases.evidence: Step 3 wait 5 s consumes 0.99999999 mmol H2O2 (O2 4.99999995e-4) before the decant, leaving H2O2 7.5e-12/2.5e-12, so post-split fractional loss is unidentifiable.
cases.next_step: Keep held as protocol-identifiability hold.

cases.title: Iodine sink changes induction time
cases.evidence: Iodine accumulates equally (I2 2.285e-5 vs 2.23e-5) while thiosulfate is consumed only by thiosulfate-acid (S solid 3.6e-5 / 7.1e-5); no I2+S2O3 sink, KI not-speciated, all absorbance 0.0 at 405 nm.
cases.next_step: Add owned I2 + 2 S2O3-2 -> 2 I- + S4O6-2 sink competing with acid decomposition, plus iodine chromophore coverage.

cases.title: Hydrolyse an ester, then oxidise the liberated alcohol
cases.evidence: Step 4 saponification: 'strong-base capacity is not established for owned CO2(aq) in Aqueous; no named hydrolysis applied'; step 6 alcohol-oxidation has nothing to act on; ethyl_acetate stays 0.001.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; carbonate reserve lane K still prerequisite
cases.next_step: Implement bounded carbonate-aware strong-base reserve (lane K) preserving seal and air carbon, then rerun original.

cases.title: Extract an esterification mixture and assay both pools
cases.evidence: Esterification gives ester 6.667e-4/ethanol 3.333e-4 with mixed-solvent boundary warning; extract refuses 'no reviewed hexane/water distribution coefficient for CH3COO-, CH3COOH and H+', receiver empty.
cases.next_step: Curate reviewed hexane/water partition data for ethyl acetate/ethanol/acetic acid with ionic exclusion.

cases.title: Serial dilution absorbance follows concentration
cases.evidence: Every UV-vis read refuses 'no absorption spectrum for copper sulfate and CuOH+'; Cu+2 stays 0.001 mol across dilutions (water 22.14 mol final).
cases.next_step: Add a reviewed Cu(II) aqua/sulfate spectrum and rerun.

cases.title: Standard addition with volume-corrected optics
cases.evidence: All spectra refuse CuSO4/CuOH+ and volume_meter refuses 'reads a sealed vessel's headspace, and this one is open'; Cu+2 final 0.001.
cases.next_step: Add Cu spectra and a liquid-volume readout (shared with QA-003).

cases.title: Conductivity changes with temperature at fixed salt
cases.evidence: Conductivity 5678.764 uS/cm at 19.95 C vs 5678.828 at 43.94 C and back to 5678.764 after cooling: essentially no temperature dependence; volume meter refuses (open vessel).
cases.next_step: Add an in-situ temperature-dependent conductivity model (or explicit reference-T compensation flag) with reviewed data.

cases.title: Chromatographic tracking of ester hydrolysis
cases.evidence: Saponification converts (final ethanol 1e-3, CH3COO- 9.998e-4); chromatograms show only an ethanol peak (rt 68.25 s) and refuse 'no curated group decomposition for ... ethyl_acetate'.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; still missing ester retention parameters
cases.next_step: Curate ethyl acetate retention/group decomposition and rerun original.

cases.title: Weaker iodine colour: dilution vs reduction
cases.evidence: Ascorbic acid reduces I2 (v1 dehydroascorbic 1e-5, HI 2e-5, colourless) while the diluted arm keeps I2 1e-5 brown, but all four spectrophotometer reads are 0.0 at 405 nm and KI is not-speciated.
cases.next_step: Add iodine/triiodide spectra and KI speciation so absorbance is nonzero or honestly refused.

cases.title: Iron-thiocyanate complex formation
cases.evidence: Steps 5/7 spectra list Fe(SCN)+2 and Fe(SCN)2+ as present but refuse 'no absorption spectrum for ... Fe(SCN)+2'; Fe total 1e-4 conserved.
cases.next_step: Add a reviewed Fe(SCN)2+ spectrum (and other Fe(III) species) to the optical model.

cases.title: Exchange AgCl for less soluble AgI
cases.evidence: Step 6 KI 6e-4 is not-speciated; AgCl(solid) remains 4.972e-4 with KI(aqueous) 6e-4 and no AgI.
cases.next_step: Map KI to K+/I- with an AgI phase in the precipitation set, then rerun original.

cases.title: Competing anions share limited barium
cases.evidence: Arm 2: 'supersaturated against Witherite (SI +2.8) ... no matching solid in this lab's registry'; only BaSO4 5e-4 precipitates and Ba+2 3e-4 stays aqueous.
cases.next_step: Register Witherite/BaCO3 solid from existing wateq4f and rerun.

cases.title: Acid selectively removes carbonate from silver precipitate
cases.evidence: Step 3: 'supersaturated against Ag2O (SI +3.6), Ag2CO3 (SI +3.1) ... no matching solid in registry'; only AgCl 3e-4 forms, so C1 (carbonate solid before acid) is inconclusive.
cases.next_step: Register Ag2CO3 (and Ag2O) solids from the existing database, then rerun.

cases.title: Titrated aliquot represents stock after volume correction
cases.evidence: Endpoint base: Na+ 1.5e-3 (v0) vs 5e-4 (v1), exactly 3:1 (C1 met); both volume_meter reads refuse 'reads a sealed vessel's headspace ... this one is open'.
cases.next_step: Provide a liquid-volume readout (or formally accept the vessel-line liquid volume) to evaluate C2.

cases.title: Carbonate/bicarbonate two-endpoint alkalinity
cases.evidence: First endpoint pH 8.3 needs 8.545 mL x 0.1 M = 0.855 mmol (forecast 0.3), T 1.004 mmol, so T-2P is negative; CO2 gas_evolved during stage 1 and QA-005 gives an almost identical P, suggesting instant open-vessel CO2 equilibration erases carbonate identity.
cases.next_step: Investigate open-vessel CO2 degassing during titration (rate-limited exchange) before any rerun.

cases.title: Hydroxide vs carbonate alkalinity
cases.evidence: P = 8.548 mL x 0.1 M = 0.855 mmol (forecast 0.7) and T = 1.004 mmol, giving OH 0.71/CO3 0.15 mmol vs 0.4/0.3; CO2 evolves already before pH 8.3.
cases.next_step: Same root cause as QA-004: model rate-limited CO2 loss in open titration, then rerun both.

cases.title: Bracket iodine endpoint with thiosulfate
cases.evidence: I2(aqueous) stays 1e-4 after 0.22 mmol thiosulfate (S2O3-2 2.2e-4 unreacted); all absorbances 0.0; KI not-speciated.
cases.next_step: Implement owned I2/thiosulfate -> iodide/tetrathionate reaction (shared iodine lane).

cases.title: Back-assay vitamin C with iodine excess
cases.evidence: Ascorbic acid consumes 0.1 mmol I2 (v1 I2 2e-4, HI 2e-4) but thiosulfate consumes nothing: blank keeps I2 3e-4 with S2O3-2 6e-4.
cases.next_step: Same iodine/thiosulfate sink as QA-007, then rerun.

cases.title: Strip iodine from organic extract by reduction
cases.evidence: Extraction works (K=85, 4.72e-5 mol to hexane) but thiosulfate 2e-4 does not reduce I2; drained water holds only I2 1.35e-6 and unreacted S2O3-2.
cases.next_step: Same owned iodine/thiosulfate sink with biphasic admission, then rerun.

cases.title: Separate nonpolar solute from soluble salt
cases.evidence: Naphthalene 5e-6 dissolved and passes the filter (C1 met), but extract refuses 'no reviewed hexane/water distribution coefficient for Cl-, Na+ and naphthalene'; organic receiver empty.
cases.next_step: Curate a reviewed naphthalene hexane/water partition (ions excluded) and rerun.

cases.title: Cooling before filtration changes recovery
cases.evidence: 0.3956 mol KNO3 (~40 g/100 g water) cooled only to 316.41 K (43 C), below saturation (~70 g/100 g), so no crystals; v2 holds all K+/NO3- 0.3956.
cases.next_step: Keep held: the original cooling dose cannot reach saturation; do not alter it.

cases.title: Distillation rejects salt but may carry volatile acid
cases.evidence: Salt arm distillate is pure water (pH 6.998, 0.055 uS/cm, NaCl rejected), but acid arm refuses 'distillation needs reviewed vapour-pressure/latent-heat properties for CH3COOH; no component was transferred'.
cases.next_step: Add reviewed acetic acid vapour-pressure/VLE and latent-heat data, then rerun.

cases.title: Selective nitrate crystallisation from mixed salts
cases.evidence: 0.4945 mol KNO3 (~50 g/100 g) cooled to 45.3 C, still undersaturated; filtrate keeps all K+ 0.4945 and Na+ 0.08555, no solids.
cases.next_step: Keep held; separately note Niter coverage at I=5.8 is unvalidated.

cases.title: Extraction recovery depends on phase ratio, not scale
cases.evidence: Both extractions refuse 'no reviewed hexane/water distribution coefficient for naphthalene'; feeds 2e-6/4e-6 remain aqueous.
cases.next_step: Curate a reviewed naphthalene partition coefficient (shared with SE-002).

cases.title: Hess-law route comparison: lime hydration
cases.evidence: Identical final Ca+2 1e-3/Cl- 2e-3, but the acid-first route calorimeter reads 5.6e-7 kJ vs 0.10382 kJ for CaO-first (103.8 J route difference).
cases.next_step: Add reviewed CaO slaking/dissolution enthalpy and verify route independence.

cases.title: Freeze concentration and lower-salt melt
cases.evidence: Cooling to -0.76 C forms ice (1.277 mol water retained, melting consumed ~7640 J of 10000 J); filtrate holds all Na+/Cl- 0.01711, but melt conductivity refuses 'no aqueous solution has been characterised'.
cases.next_step: Make the conductivity meter read pure melt water (as it does for distillate in SE-007) and formally review.

cases.title: Pressure shifts boiling plateau
cases.evidence: Regulated 200 kPa vessel boils at 100.000 C vs 99.63 C at 100 kPa (expected ~120 C); boiling_point_apparatus gives no numeric point.
cases.next_step: Use a pressure-aware water saturation curve (e.g. IAPWS via CoolProp) for regulated-pressure boiling.

cases.title: Filter does not remove dissolved dye by itself
cases.evidence: Charcoal arm filtrate methyl_orange 9.367e-7 with 1.4338e-5 adsorbed on retained charcoal (closes 1.5275e-5); filter-only control filtrate keeps 1.527e-5; spectra refuse 'finite aqueous pH is required'.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: yes; absorbance now refused instead of reading 0
cases.next_step: Formal criterion review on inventory, noting the optical gap under the coverage criterion.

cases.title: Adsorbent saturates before water becomes colourless
cases.evidence: Langmuir adsorption with finite monolayer capacity; after rescue charcoal (total 0.0333 mol) free dye is 2.287e-6 of 1.069e-4 added; spectra refused for lack of pH.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: yes; optical zero replaced by refusal
cases.next_step: Check the intermediate free-dye value after overload in raw and complete formal review.

cases.title: Recover dye from loaded adsorbent by washing
cases.evidence: First filtrate 1.646e-6 of 3.055e-5; fresh wash after stirring releases 4.159e-6 into v2, rest retained adsorbed, consistent with reversible partitioning.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: yes; optical zero replaced by refusal
cases.next_step: Verify the adsorbed pool in raw closes 3.055e-5 and do formal review.

cases.title: Two fresh adsorption stages vs one larger stage
cases.evidence: Equal 0.01665 mol charcoal: single-stage filtrate 2.788e-6 vs two-stage filtrate 7.091e-7 of 6.11e-5 dye.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: yes; optical zero replaced by refusal
cases.next_step: Verify adsorbed inventories close per stage and do formal review.

cases.title: Flame fingerprint follows the cation
cases.evidence: NaCl gives 'bright yellow', KCl 'lilac', but NaBr ignite: 'cea-thermal ... did not converge after 1 iterations' and did_not_ignite, so no signature is reported; balances stay 0.1 g.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; NaBr CEA nonconvergence persists as in prior note
cases.next_step: Make flame_test independent of CEA ignition success (cation-keyed emission) and report unparameterised salts explicitly.

cases.title: A mixture needs a mixture interpretation of its flame signal
cases.evidence: [8] mixed v3 reports only flame_test 'bright yellow' (NaCl) while inventory keeps KCl, which suits the forecast; but [6]-[8] show partial melt/freeze flapping and FINAL at T=298.15 still lists NaCl(liquid)=0.0004355 and KCl(liquid)=0.0001341.
cases.next_step: Fix phase relaxation after ignite so molten salt refreezes at 298 K, then do a formal review of the single-colour-vs-inventory criterion.

cases.title: Compare chloride, bromide and iodide precipitate fingerprints
cases.evidence: [10] AgCl precipitates 9.956e-05 mol, but [11] says 'supersaturated against Bromyrite (SI +5.4)... no matching solid in this lab's registry', and KI is 'not-speciated', so v1/v2 stay clear and look the same as the blank v3.
cases.next_step: Add an AgBr (bromyrite) registry solid and an aqueous I- mapping plus AgI solid from the existing wateq4f data, then rerun once.

cases.title: Vitamin C can hide starch from an iodine test
cases.evidence: The ascorbate/I2 ledger closes (v0 final dehydroascorbic 3e-05, I2 4e-05), but every uvvis reading is 'absorbance at 405 nm' = 0.0, including the starch+I2 positive control v1.
cases.next_step: Add a starch-triiodide optical response (with KI/I3- speciation) so the starch control gives non-zero absorbance.

cases.title: A neutral organic blend needs more than one chromatographic peak label
cases.evidence: [13] 'the column has no curated group decomposition for ethyl_acetate'; the mixture shows only ethanol (68.3 s) and propanone (114.8 s) peaks, and v3 (ester alone) has no peak.
cases.next_step: Curate an ester group decomposition and retention parameters for ethyl_acetate so all three components get predictions.

cases.title: Ionisation can change the method coverage of an organic acid
cases.evidence: [10] neutral CH3COOH is 'not-parameterised', so there is no neutral-acid peak to lose; outside_method lists CH3COO-/H+ (v0) and CH3COO-/Na+ (v1). [11] also lists 'base_equivalents' as a column species needing decomposition.
cases.next_step: Parameterise neutral acetic acid on the column, and stop passing the base_equivalents basis coordinate to the chromatograph species list.

cases.title: Triangulate a solvent identity from independent physical properties
cases.evidence: Densities are 0.789/0.785/0.7845 g/mL and boiling-point literature constants are returned, but all three melting_point reads [11]-[13] give verdict 'nothing_to_test' for these liquid stocks.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: same missing melting readouts as the prior batch3 review
cases.next_step: Let the melting-point apparatus report a curated literature constant for a liquid sample (with the same provenance boundary as boiling), or record this as an instrument hold.

cases.title: Known boundary: salt sensitivity is absent from the simple swelling model
cases.evidence: Both vessels give 'polymer_swelled' capacity_g_per_g=100, retained_water_g=20. v1 then gets NaCl at I=0.570 with no swelling update; the conductivity contrast is 0.055 vs a high-ionic reading.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: matches the prior boundary demonstration
cases.next_step: Keep it as a verified model-boundary demonstration outside the scientific count. Salt-sensitive swelling would need a separate polyelectrolyte model.

cases.title: Known boundary: emulsifying oil need not speed the aggregate lipase model
cases.evidence: Only v0 (soap) reports emulsion_changed (to_dispersed_fraction 0.552). Both vessels have identical enzyme_hydrolysed converted_fraction 0.01102 (stir) and 0.49138 (wait), so the rate does not depend on interfacial area.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: matches the prior boundary demonstration
cases.next_step: Keep it as a boundary demonstration and do not add it to the scientific count.

cases.title: An irradiation command is not proof of a supported photochemical pathway
cases.evidence: [10]/[11] 'irradiated' with photolysis_coupled=false. H2O2 in irradiated v0 and the dark control v1 is the same (9.951e-05), and the pressures are identical (101.3234 kPa).
cases.next_step: Formally review the criteria. Note that it is a boundary demonstration and may belong outside the scientific count like BD001/002/004.

cases.title: A missing chromatographic peak does not prove a missing ingredient
cases.evidence: The chromatogram shows an ethanol peak with outside_method ['Cl-','Na+'], but albumin (unresolved_amount 0.188 g) is not labelled. The balance reads 39.9965 g, which omits the 0.188 g unresolved protein.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: the same unresolved-mass readback undercount as the prior notes
cases.next_step: Fix the balance/readback so it includes unresolved material mass, and have the chromatograph list unresolved material as outside the method.

cases.title: Separate light scattering from a dissolved pigment signal
cases.evidence: status=refused: 'centrifuge rotor is 60.09 g out of balance (sample 39.91 g, counterbalance 100.00 g)'. Before that, milk alone reads absorbance 0.0 at 405 nm, so no scattering is represented.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: same counterbalance refusal; a prior 39.91 g follow-up reached the centrifuge
cases.next_step: Use the already-preserved 39.91 g counterbalance follow-up for the centrifuge step. Turbidity/scattering optics stays a separate instrument gap.

cases.title: Foam volume is not the number of moles of gas
cases.evidence: Total CO2 is comparable: v0 1.34e-4 + 8.65e-4 mol, v1 the same. Only v0 (soap) reports foam_changed: trapped_gas_liters 0.0045, then 0.00357, then 0.00142, with no CO2 returning to bicarbonate.
cases.next_step: Formally review the criteria, and check that citrate is all C6H5O7-3 at pH 6.1 while a 2e-4 'H+' pool is carried.

cases.title: Starch digestion: sample before adding the iodine indicator
cases.evidence: Amylase turns all starch into maltose 0.0006168 at the moment it is added [4], but all three uvvis reads are 'absorbance at 405 nm' 0.0, including the intact-starch control v1.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: the same zero-405 nm optical hold as the prior AD001/EN001 review
cases.next_step: Add the starch-triiodide optical coupling. Also review the instant (time-independent) amylase conversion and the maltose 'no-solver' dissolution.

cases.title: Lactase acts on the milk substrate pool, not on free glucose
cases.evidence: Only milk v0 reports enzyme_hydrolysed lactase converted_fraction 0.2979. The glucose control v2 has no conversion. Milk carries 'uncompensated ionic charge... adjusts pH' boundaries.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no: same narrow conversion pass and milk charge/pH hold
cases.next_step: Resolve the milk-matrix charge/pH authority (casein buffer, analytical charge) under the milk physical closure lane before qualifying.

cases.title: Selective digestion in a mixed milk-and-gelatin matrix
cases.evidence: The selectivity is correct: lactase gives fraction 0.5070 on milk, protease gives 0.9072 on gelatine, and v2 gets both separately. Milk 'uncompensated ionic charge' boundary events remain.
cases.next_step: Close the milk charge/pH hold, and recheck the earlier 1.4e-10 formal-charge residual against the strict ledger.

cases.title: Molecular products and aggregate conversion are different outputs
cases.evidence: v0 starch 0.0012335 becomes maltose 0.0006168 (molecular), and the balance stays 50.0600 g before and after. v1 is only a lactase annotation (fraction 0.5070), and its balance stays 40.0500 g.
cases.next_step: Do a formal criterion review, and decide whether the milk charge/pH hold applies (it should not, since only representation and mass are asked).

cases.title: Sugar conversion can occur without gas production
cases.evidence: In yeast v0, sucrose -0.002616 gives CO2 0.010465 and ethanol 0.010465, at 147.6 kPa. In yoghurt v1 there is lactic 0.000262 + lactate 4.4e-05 with no CO2 and 99.66 kPa, which matches the sugar-only control v2 (99.66 kPa).
cases.next_step: Do a formal criterion review, including closure of the C/H/O ledger.

cases.title: Sourdough allocates carbon to acid, alcohol and gas
cases.evidence: v1 has ethanol 0.002442, lactic+lactate 0.002442 and CO2 0.00245 (gas+aq) from sucrose -0.001221, which closes carbon (12 x 0.001221 = 6 x 0.00244). The chromatogram shows only ethanol and labels lactate/sucrose not-parameterised.
cases.next_step: Formally review the criteria. Note that the 'fermented' event under-describes the lactic share even though the ledger closes.

cases.title: Compare fresh and dry yeast on a dry-solids basis
cases.evidence: The solids match: active yeast is 0.2774 g in v0 vs 0.2768 g in v1, compared with 0.0832 g in v2. But the open vessels report 'gas_absorbed' for all produced CO2, keep CO2(aq) 0.00168, and the balance rises to 50.85 g.
cases.next_step: Fix the fermentation CO2 ownership in open vessels so produced gas can vent rather than being treated as a finite dose that is fully absorbed.

cases.title: A two-stage sugar-to-acid bioprocess
cases.evidence: Stage 1 gives ethanol 0.004954. After the acetobacter and O2 additions, CH3COOH+CH3COO- is 0.001235, O2 goes from 0.007211 to 0.005976 (-0.001235), and ethanol is 0.005833 - 0.004598 = 0.001235, so all three agree.
cases.next_step: Do a formal review of the oxygen/ethanol/acid reconciliation and residual yeast activity.

cases.title: Yeast does not make starch an automatically fermentable sugar
cases.evidence: Sucrose v0 ferments (CO2 0.007908, 135.9 kPa). Starch v1 stays starch(solid)=0.006168 with no gas (99.66 kPa).
cases.next_step: Do a formal criterion review.

cases.title: The milk matrix changes what acidification can tell you
cases.evidence: Lactic stock is about the same (milk 0.00169 vs sugar 0.00168), but the pH is 4.62 in milk and 2.65 in sugar. The milk carries the 'uncompensated ionic charge' boundary, and the vessels cool from 40 C to 25 C.
cases.next_step: Resolve the milk pH/buffer authority under the milk physical closure lane. Do not change the thermostat.

cases.title: An oxygen pulse can restart a limited acetification step
cases.evidence: The first pulse is fully used (O2 total_after on the second add is 0.0005). Final O2 is 0.0001826, and acetic acid+acetate is 0.000586, which equals the O2 consumed and the ethanol lost (0.001 - 0.000414).
cases.next_step: Do a formal criterion review, including the stage-1 inspect increments.

cases.title: Cold storage followed by warming is a history, not a new culture
cases.evidence: Cold v0 drifts from 5 C to 25 C during the first 4 h (pH 4.98). The heat gives 59.8 C, and afterwards pH is 3.35 with lactic total 9.45e-05, against the warm control's 3.88e-04 (pH 3.02). No culture is added.
cases.next_step: Formally review the per-stage conversion increments using measured temperatures. Note the unthermostatted cold leg.

cases.title: A baking-powder formulation is not just sodium bicarbonate
cases.evidence: The baking powder releases only NaHCO3 and starch (unresolved 0.225 g). CO2 is identical to bicarbonate alone (0.000406 cold, 0.000360 heated), with no leavening-acid reaction or not_yet_modeled notice.
cases.next_step: Add a resolved heat-activated leavening acid (e.g. SAPP) to the recipe with a supported reaction, or emit an explicit unsupported-component notice.

cases.title: An antioxidant response is not a food-safety verdict
cases.evidence: The browning_changed fraction is lower with ascorbate (0.491 vs 0.982 at 30 min), but every 'look' at v0 says 'There is nothing to see in the beaker', so the browning is never visible. Ascorbic acid stays solid at 0.0001.
cases.next_step: Have the eyes/scene readback render cut-apple material and its browned fraction, and check why each wait emits two browning events.

cases.title: A formulation can contain both a gas source and a starch-test target
cases.evidence: The baking powder contributes starch(solid)=0.0007709 in v1, but both uvvis reads are 0.0 absorbance at 405 nm, so starch-iodine gives no signal. KI is 'not-speciated'.
cases.next_step: Same starch-triiodide optical coupling as AN004/EN001.

cases.title: Two natural pigments can share a colour without sharing a spectrum
cases.evidence: [11] chlorophyll/ethanol absorbance at 405 nm = 0.0 despite 5e-7 mol dissolved; [12] betanin 525 nm = 1.04; blanks [13],[14] = 0.0.
cases.changed_since_prior_notes: no; chlorophyll band still absent as in prior hold
cases.next_step: Add a curated chlorophyll-a ethanol spectrum (Soret/Q bands) with provenance, then rerun the original unchanged.

cases.title: Curcumin colour and a neutral solvent blank
cases.evidence: Blank [7]/[13] = 0.0 at 405 nm (meets blank clause); curcumin 425 nm 1.1 -> 1.1000024 after Na2CO3 raises pH to 10.115 with no band shift.
cases.next_step: Curate a pH-dependent (enolate) curcumin spectrum in mixed solvent or have the instrument declare pH-coverage absence explicitly.

cases.title: A sunscreen model has spectral bands, not one universal shield factor
cases.evidence: [7] UV-B and [8] UV-A emit uv_attenuated events; [9] 550 nm gives only 'irradiated' with no attenuation/transmission output; water control has none.
cases.next_step: Add a declared visible-band transmission readout (or explicit out-of-domain event) for the sunscreen recipe.

cases.title: Heating does not increase every mineral solubility
